examples.en: The company diversified its products and customers increased.
The restaurant decided to diversify its menu.
It's safer to diversify your sources of income.
The school is diversifying its teaching methods.
To diversify the customer base, we need promotion.
After I diversified my investments, the risk went down.

explain: 방식, 상품, 종류 같은 것을 여러 가지로 늘릴 때 써요. 뉴스나 회사 이야기에서 많이 나오는 딱딱한 말이라 일상에서는 '다양하게 하다'라고 풀어 말하기도 해요. '다양해지다'는 저절로 여러 가지가 되는 것이에요.
explain_en: It is used when you expand something such as methods, products or types into more varieties. It's a formal word common in news and business, so in daily talk people may say '다양하게 하다'. '다양해지다' means becoming varied on its own.

examples.en: There is a small hourglass on the desk.
When you flip the hourglass, the time starts again.
I time boiling ramyeon with a three-minute hourglass.
The sand in the hourglass has almost all fallen.
I received a pretty hourglass as a gift.

examples.ko: 게임에서 모래시계 표시가 보이면 기다려야 해요.
examples.en: In a game, you have to wait when you see the hourglass icon.

explain: 모래시계는 모래가 떨어지는 시간을 보는 도구인데, 컴퓨터 화면에서 '기다리세요'를 뜻하는 표시도 그렇게 불러요. 몸매를 말할 때 '모래시계 몸매'처럼 쓰기도 하지만 외모 이야기라 조심해서 써야 해요.
explain_en: 모래시계 is a tool for measuring time by falling sand, and the 'please wait' icon on a computer screen is called by the same name. '모래시계 몸매' is used for a body shape, but since it is about looks, use it with care.

examples.en: It took a year for that idea to become a product.
They are turning local specialties into products and selling them.
When the character became popular, it was turned into merchandise right away.

examples.ko: 상품화에 성공하면 큰돈을 벌 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the productization succeeds, you can make a lot of money.
This technology hasn't been turned into a product yet.
The design changed a lot during the productization process.

explain: 아이디어, 기술, 캐릭터 같은 것을 팔 수 있는 물건이나 서비스로 만드는 것을 말해요. '상업화'보다 중립적이고, 비판하는 느낌은 적어요. 보통 '상품화하다/상품화되다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It means turning an idea, technology or character into a product or service that can be sold. It is more neutral than '상업화' and carries less criticism. Typical forms are '상품화하다' and '상품화되다'.

en: use regularly; be a regular user of

examples.en: I use this cafe regularly.

examples.ko: 많은 사람들이 이 앱을 애용하고 있어요.
examples.en: Many people use this app regularly.

examples.ko: 친구가 애용하는 화장품을 저도 사 봤어요.
examples.en: I also tried buying the cosmetics my friend uses regularly.
If you use public transportation often, it is good for the environment too.
Grandmother used this herb regularly for a long time.

examples.ko: 자주 애용했던 가게가 문을 닫아서 아쉬워요.
examples.en: It's a pity that the shop I used to visit often closed.

explain: '쓰다'나 '이용하다'보다 마음에 들어서 계속 찾는 느낌이에요. 가게, 서비스, 교통수단 앞에서 많이 써요. '많이 애용해 주세요'라는 안내 문구를 자주 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: Compared with 쓰다 or 이용하다, it suggests you like something and keep going back to it. It is common with shops, services, and transport. You often see the notice 많이 애용해 주세요.

examples.ko: 제야의 종소리를 들으러 많은 사람이 모였어요.
examples.en: Many people gathered to hear the bell-ringing on New Year's Eve.

examples.ko: 올해는 제야에 친구들과 해돋이 여행을 떠났어요.
examples.en: This year I left on a sunrise trip with friends on New Year's Eve.
Fireworks filled the night sky on New Year's Eve.
The news broadcasts the New Year's Eve event live.

examples.ko: 저는 제야에 한 해를 돌아보며 일기를 써요.
examples.en: On New Year's Eve I look back on the year and write in my diary.

examples.ko: 제야의 종을 치는 순간 모두 새해 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: The moment the bell was struck, everyone exchanged New Year greetings.

explain: 12월 31일 밤을 가리키는데, 일상 대화에서는 '새해 전날'이나 '12월 31일'이라고 더 많이 말해요. '제야의 종'처럼 굳은 표현이나 뉴스에서 주로 만나요. 새해를 맞는 날은 '새해 첫날'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means the night of December 31, but in daily talk people usually say '새해 전날' or '12월 31일'. You mostly meet it in set phrases like '제야의 종' and in the news. The day that follows is called '새해 첫날'.
